headline: High: shared workspace plus broad tool access creates prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk; Notion AI is safer but still exposed through shared content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI ingests workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while oh-my-openagent can use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and read AGENTS.md/README.md. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if shared workspace files or prompts are exchanged. The pair is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward from low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace files or notes, injected instructions can cross from B into A.
IF B is configured to parse repository text as agent instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Restrict B to a separate workspace directory.
Disable automatic ingestion of AGENTS.md/README.md as instructions in B.
Use a manual review step before A consumes any B-authored text.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared documents.
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents with separate storage roots.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content and sends data to vendor backends; B touches project code, session history, and provider authentication data with broad network egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive content can flow from A into B's outputs or from B into third-party services. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A and B share the same workspace or account context, workspace content can be exposed to both.
IF B is given provider auth data from the same environment, it can transmit that data over broad egress.
mitigations: Separate accounts and OAuth principals.
Keep B away from any workspace containing secrets or regulated data.
Disable B network access except to approved endpoints.
Review A outputs before copying them into B.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has shared workspace state across instances and can access workspace pages/databases; B has broad network egress, subprocesses, browsers, and runtime-injected MCPs/hooks. Even though A cannot write files, B can mutate local config and external resources while A reads shared content, so conflicting actions on shared mutable state are plausible. Uncertainty about exact overlap escalates severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, B can change files while A reads stale content.
IF B uses hooks or MCPs to mutate shared resources, concurrent writes can race with A's workspace reads.
mitigations: Run the agents on separate directories.
Pause one agent while the other edits shared state.
Disable B hooks for shared resources.
Use version control or snapshots before B runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspace mutations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a RAG-style Q&A agent grounded in workspace content, and B can create tasks/messages and act through tools. If B treats A's generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. A does not have verified action authority, so this is not high, but the default tool-rich B makes the pathway real.
conditions: IF B consumes A's summaries without verification, hallucinations can propagate into tasks or messages.
IF A's workspace-grounded answer is used as a source for B actions, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source files.
Mark A outputs as untrusted drafts.
Add a human approval step before B sends messages or creates tasks.
Limit B actions to read-only mode for sensitive workflows.
requires-engineering: implement citation checking before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: A is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion vendor backends, while B handles provider auth prompts and broad network egress. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets enters the shared workflow, residency and retention controls may diverge. The profiles do not document a specific regulatory mismatch, so this remains a medium compliance risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into A's workspace content, it may be processed by vendor backends.
IF B is used in an environment with residency or retention requirements, its broad egress can violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings before use.
Disable B on projects with compliance constraints.
Log and review outbound destinations for B.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
